problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}2x\,\text{d}s,$ where $C$ is the ellipse $4{x}^{2}+16{y}^{2}=64,$ traversed once in the counterclockwise direction?

activity_context.topic_title: Line Integrals of Scalar Functions Over Ellipses

feedback.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}({x}^{2}-8{y}^{2})\,\text{d}s,$ where $C$ is the ellipse ${x}^{2}+8{y}^{2}=8,$ traversed once in the counterclockwise direction?
feedback.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}s={\int }_{a}^{b}f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t.
$$

 

Note that we can write the equation of our ellipse in the form

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{(2\sqrt{2})^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{1}^{2}}=1.
$$

So, the curve $C$ is an ellipse centered at $O$ with horizontal and vertical semiaxes of $2\sqrt{2}$ and $1,$ respectively. Therefore, it can be parametrized as 

$$
r(t)=⟨2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,\,0\le t<2\pi .
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖,$ we get following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)j \\  & =-2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{8{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{7{sin}^{2}⁡t+({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\sqrt{7{sin}^{2}⁡t+1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)={x}^{2}-8{y}^{2},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =(2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}-8(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2} \\  & =8{cos}^{2}⁡t-8{sin}^{2}⁡t \\  & =8({cos}^{2}⁡t-{sin}^{2}⁡t) \\  & =8\operatorname{cos}⁡2t.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}({x}^{2}-8{y}^{2})\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }8\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\sqrt{7{sin}^{2}⁡t+1}\,\text{d}t \\  & =8{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\sqrt{7{sin}^{2}⁡t+1}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$
